keyframe_review.note: 151,479 km2 for 1956-1957 against the infobox 163,610 km2 (no year given; ratio 0.93, inside the factor-of-two check; the difference is water and the grid). The whole country from 20 March 1956; the French naval base at Bizerte stayed French until 15 October 1963 (Bizerte crisis page) but is drawn as Tunisian here, as it is in every Cliopatria shape.

151,652 km2 for 1958-1962, 0.1 percent above the 1956 shape. No page opened ties a land change to 1958; the difference is read as grid noise. The republic was declared in 1957 (rename event), not 1958.

151,479 km2 for 1963-1972. The Bizerte base was handed over on 15 October 1963 ('The French finally handed Bizerte over on 15 October 1963'): the ledger's 1963 gain is the only dated border event; the Algerian border became an international one in 1962 without a change of line (Algeria-Tunisia border page).

151,578 km2 for 1973-1975, the same land as the neighbouring shapes within 0.1 percent. The Libya-Tunisia land border is the 1910 line ('A treaty of 19 May 1910 then delimited the border in greater detail'); no page opened dates a change in 1973.

151,479 km2 for 1976-2023. The 1982 ICJ continental-shelf decision 'in favor of Libya' concerns the sea, not the land shape; 'Currently, there are no new discussions between the stakeholders on the final demarcation of the border.'
151,479 km2, the same as 1976-2023; Tunisia has the same land at the end of the record ('bordered by Algeria on the west (965 km) and southwest and Libya on the south east (459 km)').

region.text: Tunisia, the territory of the French protectorate

ledger.note: 1956: Tunisia becomes independent from France under Habib Bourguiba. 'Tunisia achieved independence from France on 20 March 1956 with Habib Bourguiba as Prime Minister.'

1957: Tunisia is declared a republic with Bourguiba as first President. 'A year later, Tunisia was declared a republic, with Bourguiba as the first President.' The infobox date is 25 July 1957 (taken from the fetch summary of the infobox). The state, its land and its colour continue (rule 2); the dossier keeps one slug for the state of 1956-57 and the republic.

region.text: the French naval base at Bizerte, on Tunisian soil: Tunisia blockaded it 'hoping to force its evacuation'

ledger.note: 1961: fighting over the French naval base at Bizerte begins. Infobox dates the crisis '19 July 1961 – 15 October 1963'. The page names the base, not its boundary; the 15 km radius is the researcher's reading.
1963: France leaves Bizerte. 'The French finally handed Bizerte over on 15 October 1963, after the conclusion of the Algerian War.'

region.text: the Bizerte base, 'Evacuation of the Bizerte base on 15 October 1963' (infobox territorial changes)

ledger.note: 15 October 1963: the French evacuate Bizerte and the base returns to Tunisia. Cliopatria draws the base as Tunisian from 1956, so the renderer should treat this as a small outlined gain on land already coloured; the extent of the base is the researcher's reading.

wars.name: Bizerte crisis

zones.text: the French naval base at Bizerte

wars.outcome: Infobox 'French victory' in the fighting of July 1961, but France handed the Bizerte base to Tunisia on 15 October 1963.
wars.note: Infobox period 19 July 1961 - 15 October 1963. The page does not name the sectors fought over beyond the base.

certainty.note: Land frontiers are colonial delimitations: the Libya line by 'A treaty of 19 May 1910', marked 1910-11; the Algeria line by French decrees of 1888-89 and 1901 and southern sections 'delimited during the period 1911-23', confirmed by 'an agreement of 6 January 1960'. The exception is the Bizerte base, French-held until 15 October 1963.

Treaty lines on both land borders; the sea border with Libya was decided by the ICJ in 1982 (confirmed 1985) and the Libya-Tunisia border page says 'Currently, there are no new discussions between the stakeholders on the final demarcation of the border.'

notes: Cliopatria: six shapes 1956-2024, all 151,479-151,652 km2 on the same bbox (7.54-11.62 E, 30.31-37.32 N); the differences (0.1 percent) are grid noise and no page opened explains them. Infobox 163,610 km2 (no year). Wikidata: Q948 is Tunisia's own id; the brief's collision list does not mention it. Predecessor: the French protectorate of Tunisia (the colonial state before 20 March 1956) has no Cliopatria row after the Beylik of Tunis ends in 1884; french-africa is named as counterpart because it is the Cliopatria colonial shape alive in 1956-1957 next to Tunisia; the af-08 french-africa and protectorate dossiers should carry the matching loss. A page 'French protectorate of Tunisia' was not opened (page budget). Bizerte: the French base is the only dated territorial event; its extent is not on the page, so the 15 km radius is a reading. Rulers: the Tunisia article gives Bourguiba (1957-1987), Ben Ali (1987 to 14 January 2011) and Saied (from 23 October 2019) with dates but not the start or end of Marzouki and Essebsi, so no ruler strip is written. Pages that said nothing: History of Tunisia (text ended in the 9th century). Not found: Sakiet Sidi Youssef 1958, Gafsa 1980 (pages not opened).
